prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit with composition refinement. Edit the provided AshenSpire Starstone Pebble card painting into a polished second pass. Remove the entire blank parchment strip and ALL paper, labels, plaques or banner-like shapes; replace that area naturally with the scene. Recompose as a SQUARE 1:1 painting intended to fill a square card illustration well. Preserve the original ruined Observatory setting, worn brown leather glove, abandoned brass astronomical instruments, ash-grey masonry, cool restrained palette and textured dark-fantasy painted finish. Simplify and soften the background substantially so it cannot compete with the spell. Make the object clearly a pebble: ONE small irregular rounded dark meteoric stone, approximately thumb-tip sized in world scale, with tiny blue-white starry fissures, NOT a tall faceted crystal or giant rock. It hovers just above the gloved palm. Move the camera closer so palm and stone form a compact, unmistakable focal silhouette in the central half of the square. A concentrated blue-white light around the pebble throws attractive cold rim light across the fingertips and leather creases; one short, controlled arc of starlight makes the tiny stone read at card size. Keep the important stone and hand features between 25 and 70 percent of canvas height so title and rule panel do not obscure them. Show an anatomically credible hand with natural fingers. Rich hand-painted surfaces and confident brushwork, not photorealism, not neon or a sci-fi hologram. No lettering, symbols, numbers, captions, borders, card UI, parchment, watermark, logo or extra floating stones. Opaque full background. The result should feel like a humble but potent first sorcery, with much clearer focal hierarchy than the original.
